add.issue.name: Attachments 1: events, media storage, ingest validation

edit.description.md:
Phase 1 core (see image-attachments.plan.md).

- New events: `add.issue.attachment` {issue, hash, ext, name, bytes} and `delete.issue.attachment` — metadata only, blobs never enter the log
- Blobs at `.epiq/media/<sha256>.<ext>` in the state worktree (same branch as events → atomic sync)
- Blobs are immutable, never deleted (peek/replay must render history); delete removes the reference only
- Ingest validation: magic-byte sniffing, whitelist png/jpg/gif/webp (no SVG), recompute sha256 must match filename, bytes ≤ cap
- Materialize into issue `attachments[]`; update getAffectedNodeIds
- Verify sync.ts stages media files, not just events/

add.issue.name: Attachments 1: API upload + serve endpoints

edit.description.md:
Phase 1 core (see image-attachments.plan.md).

- POST /api/attachments — JSON {issue, name, dataBase64}; decode → validate → hash → write blob → persist event → broadcast via websocket
- GET /media/<hash>.<ext> — static serve from state worktree, correct Content-Type, Cache-Control: immutable
- Path regex `^[a-f0-9]{64}\.(png|jpe?g|gif|webp)$` (no traversal)
- Delete via existing event/command path

add.issue.name: Timeline layout modes: even frames (default) vs real-time spacing

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent): the scrubber currently spaces frames by real elapsed time, which leaves "empty void" gaps where no activity happened. Add two toggleable layout modes:

1. **Real spacing** (current behavior) — frames positioned proportionally to actual time elapsed, gaps visible where history is quiet.
2. **Even frames** (new, becomes the default) — every non-empty bucket gets equal width, laid out as a contiguous stacked filmstrip with no gaps, regardless of real time between them.

Needs a UI control to toggle between the two modes. Default mode changes from the current always-real-spacing behavior to even-frames.

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent):
1. Remove the "History" label to the left of the timeline — user wants a rich, uncluttered history to demo.
2. Move all other elements (read-only banner, mode toggle buttons, hover/"Now" label) so they sit above the timeline track, rather than inline beside it — so they never push/resize the scrubber track when they appear or disappear (e.g. the read-only banner showing up while scrubbing).
3. Rename the "Real time" toggle option to something better than "Real time" — user suggested "Timeline" as a candidate. Landed on "Frames" (even, gapless filmstrip) vs "Timeline" (true chronological/proportional spacing) as the pair.

Standing instruction reaffirmed: every new user request gets documented here as a ticket (or via comments/description), not just tracked internally.

add.issue.name: Scrubber: pick frame resolution/scope (week/month/year) with an offset to page through history

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent): "can we make it so that you can pick the resolution for the frame view, and the scope of the timeline? so 'week' 'month', 'year', and an offset, so that if you have a long history you can be more precise?"

Plan:
- Scope selector: All / Week / Month / Year (calendar-aligned periods).
- Offset control (prev/next) to page backward through history at that scope (offset 0 = current period).
- Server's getEventTimeline already buckets into ~300 slices across whatever window it's given — narrowing the window (a week vs all-time) naturally increases resolution/precision for free, no separate resolution knob needed. Extend it to accept an explicit {start, end} window instead of always defaulting to [earliest event, now].
- Websocket protocol: timeline:get gains an optional {start, end} payload.
- Client: TimeScrubber owns scope+offset state, computes the calendar period bounds, and re-requests the timeline whenever they change.

add.issue.comment.md: Correction from user: "what I mean is: make it so that you can pick interval as a rolling window." I had implemented calendar-aligned periods (Mon–Sun weeks, 1st-of-month, Jan 1 years) — wrong assumption. Switching to true rolling windows: offset 0 = the most recent N days ending now, offset 1 = the N days before that, etc. — plain duration arithmetic from "now", not calendar-boundary snapping.

add.issue.name: Frame resolution too coarse when zoomed into Week/Month scope

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent, with screenshot): "for a week the resolution of the frame is too low. I want the resolution of the frames to become more fine as you zoom in, so you can be more specific..."

Root cause: `TIMELINE_BUCKET_COUNT = 300` in epiq-time-travel.ts is a fixed constant applied to whatever window is requested, so a "week" scope buckets at ~33.6 minutes/slot — coarse enough that a burst of activity within an hour collapses into 1-2 giant Frames-mode blocks.

Fix: the bucketing loop iterates over events, not over bucket slots (Map only ever holds as many entries as non-empty buckets, bounded by real event count) — so bucket count is essentially free to increase. Raise TIMELINE_BUCKET_COUNT substantially so resolution scales down to seconds for narrow scopes without any performance or payload-size cost.

add.issue.name: Fix: autosync clobbers time-travel checkout via a TOCTOU race (getGuiState() re-check after async sync)

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent): "when I check out old state I keep geting sent back to live state. I think this is because there is some sync happening even if I am in detached 'read only state'... can you investigate..."

Root cause confirmed: `source/gui/api/lib/api-autosync.ts`'s `runSync()` checks `getTimeTravelStatus().mode !== 'live'` only ONCE, before `await sync({repoRoot})` — a real network git pull/push that can take anywhere from tens of ms to seconds. `sync()` itself doesn't touch the state singleton (confirmed by reading `mcp/epiq-api.ts`'s `sync` export — it's pure git pull/push + sync-status bookkeeping). But immediately after it resolves, `runSync` unconditionally calls `getGuiState()` (which `boot()`s — unconditionally re-materializes live state from the event log) and broadcasts the result to every client, with no re-check. If a `time-travel:scrub` websocket message is processed during that async gap (fully plausible — the 15s interval fires regardless of user activity), the historical checkout gets silently overwritten and broadcast back to live the moment the in-flight sync finishes. This also likely explains the "stale/wrong state on first load" flakiness observed repeatedly during earlier manual browser testing this session, previously (incorrectly) written off as a browser-automation timing artifact.

Fix: a proper async mutex shared between checkoutStateAt/returnToLive (epiq-time-travel.ts) and runSync (api-autosync.ts) so the two operations can never interleave — whichever starts first runs to completion (including its broadcast) before the other begins, and each re-reads the live/scrub mode fresh at the moment it actually acquires the lock rather than trusting a stale pre-await check.

add.issue.comment.md:
Found a broader instance of the same bug while verifying the autosync fix: `getGuiState()` (mcp/epiq-api.ts) unconditionally calls `boot()` — re-materializing live state — on every call, and it's called from more than just autosync: `websocket.ts`'s `state:get` handler (fires on every client connect/reconnect, and via the client's `requestState()` retry path), plus several api-server.ts HTTP endpoints including the plain GET `/api/state`. Any of these firing while scrubbing would silently clobber the checkout the same way autosync did — a client reconnect alone (e.g. a network blip) would be enough, no sync required.

Fixing at the source: make `getGuiState()` itself skip `boot()` and fall back to `deriveGuiState()` when time-travel mode isn't live, so every call site is safe automatically instead of relying on each caller to remember to guard.
